source.title: Electrophysiological evidence for target facilitation without distractor suppression in two-stimulus search displays

confidence_rationale: Directly tests and fails to find the central prediction of the signal suppression hypothesis using two independent converging measures with an appropriate task-irrelevant filler baseline. Weakens the premise that a proactive PRE-selection suppression signal is required, which is the premise Q-082 interrogates. Held below 0.75 because it is a null result in a deliberately minimal two-item display, where competition may be too weak to require suppression.
failure_signatures: No early proactive suppression of highly salient distractors was detectable below the task-irrelevant filler baseline -- the pattern was initial capture by ALL colour-change items followed by later focusing on the target, i.e. facilitation, not suppression.

A null result in a two-item display may not generalise to higher set sizes where competition is stronger; an architecture that reads this as 'no suppression substrate needed' may fail as the number of competing candidates grows -- directly relevant to whether MECH-254's top-k bottleneck scales.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Using steady-state visual evoked potentials and lateralised alpha as concurrent indices of attentional allocation, with task-irrelevant filler stimuli as the critical baseline, the study found no evidence that salient distractors are proactively suppressed below the filler level; instead all colour-change stimuli initially captured attention and the target was subsequently focused upon.
mapping.ree_translation: REE reads this as evidence for the second horn of Q-082. If the human data do not require a proactive pre-selection suppression signal even for highly salient distractors, and the observed pattern is competition followed by target upweighting, then REE's existing precision-weighted cue routing plus the top-k boundary bottleneck may already be the right shape, and no explicit suppression substrate is owed.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a NULL result, and the display had only two items -- competition may simply be too weak at set size two to recruit suppression that appears at larger set sizes. Absence of a detectable SSVEP/alpha suppression signature is also not absence of suppression, since both measures are coarse relative to single-unit competition. The finding constrains the strength of the affirmative case for Q-082; it does not settle the question negatively, and Q-082 remains gated on MECH-467 leg 3 regardless.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adult humans, EEG (steady-state visual evoked potentials and endogenous alpha), two-item visual search displays with colour-singleton distractors and task-irrelevant filler stimuli embedded in a flickering stream.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality good -- two converging electrophysiological measures and, crucially, the filler baseline that lets suppression BELOW baseline be distinguished from mere relative de-prioritisation. Discounted as a null result in a minimal display.
